name: pike-marketfront
summary:
I changed the generator (parts/shell0, towers, plot1, plaza), re-ran it and saved the result as build.nbt. 7,283 cells changed from v1.nbt.
MarketFront: the exposed tier walls are now light grey panels with a charcoal panel every 3rd bay, a stripped-spruce fin every 5 blocks and a charcoal band under each deck. Spruce decking strips run across the plaza. The housing's north, south and east faces got timber fins and lit 3x2 windows. I removed the west stair tower and replaced the twin Pike St towers with one low glass kiosk.
Hillclimb: the elevator tower has solid concrete back walls from the ground up. Lanterns stand on every terrace and plaza rail post.

revisions.comment:
Fix round on the composed views. Keep footprints, plots, site orientation and the ground levels. Fix:
1. MarketFront reads as a jumble of grey boxes. Make it one coherent modern market pavilion stepping down the bluff: at the top (Pike Place level, high x) a broad open rooftop plaza in light stone and wood decking with planters, benches, glass railings and a bronze pig; below it two or three clear tiers toward the bay (low x), each a long band of glass storefronts and windows under a warm wood soffit, the walls in light grey and charcoal panels with vertical timber fins. Fewer, bigger, cleaner volumes; no stray tower stubs.
2. The hillclimb plot has a piece floating in the air (an elevator/stair tower block standing above nothing). Everything must stand on the ground per the ground map: the terraces step down with the slope, the elevator tower rises from the lowest terrace with its glass shaft, and the stairs connect terrace to terrace.
3. Lights for dusk: warm glow in the storefront glass, lanterns along the terraces and the plaza.
revisions.summary:
I changed the generator (parts/shell0, towers, plot1, plaza), re-ran it and saved the result as build.nbt. 7,283 cells changed from v1.nbt.
MarketFront: the exposed tier walls are now light grey panels with a charcoal panel every 3rd bay, a stripped-spruce fin every 5 blocks and a charcoal band under each deck. Spruce decking strips run across the plaza. The housing's north, south and east faces got timber fins and lit 3x2 windows. I removed the west stair tower and replaced the twin Pike St towers with one low glass kiosk.
Hillclimb: the elevator tower has solid concrete back walls from the ground up. Lanterns stand on every terrace and plaza rail post.
applied: 1. Fewer volumes, no stray tower stubs: removed the west stair tower (it rose 7 blocks above the plaza on the west face). The two tall glass towers at the Pike St end are now one 8-high glass kiosk with a flat cap.

1. Wall skin: the end and side walls of every tier are now light grey and charcoal concrete panels with a vertical stripped-spruce fin every 5 blocks and a charcoal band under the deck. The housing's north, south and east faces have fins every 7 blocks and 3x2 glass windows with warm light behind them, so the whole building uses one set of materials.
1. Rooftop plaza: three spruce-plank decking strips now run through the stone deck (x 80-82, 94-96, 106-108 in plot coordinates). The planters, benches, glass rails and bronze pig are unchanged.
1. Glass storefronts under the wood soffit: the long west-facing glass bands with their timber canopies were already there, and I left them as they were.

2. Floating piece: the elevator tower's footing was already on the ground, so nothing was actually hanging. Its glass renders see-through, though, which leaves only the floor bands and cap visible, and that reads as a block in the air. I made its east and south back walls solid concrete from its base at y 4 up to the cap, with smooth-stone bands at each terrace level. The glass shaft and doorways stay on the west and north faces. check reports 0 floating blocks.

2. Terraces step down with the slope, and stairs run terrace to terrace: both were already true. The terraces sit on the ground map at decks 2, 9, 16 and 23, and three flights connect them, so I didn't change them.
3. Lanterns: 38 on the terrace rail posts in plot 1 and 32 on the plaza's glass-rail posts, on top of the existing lamp posts.
3. Warm glow in the glass: the existing glow strip behind the storefront glass (1,332 lit cells, 75 lanterns, 108 candles) is kept. I added warm froglight behind the new housing windows.
skipped: The elevator tower does not stand on the lowest terrace. It stays on its planned spot (x 63-71, z 48-59) at ground level 4. That spot is next to the upper terraces, not on the waterfront landing, and moving it would have changed the plot layout.

The Pike St kiosk still sits on its own small patch of ground (its map ground is 19-24), so in a standalone render it looks like an island. In the composed site the real terrain should surround it. I can't confirm that, because I didn't re-render the composed views.
The housing block and the old white-brick market building are unchanged apart from the housing's fins and windows. The brief asks for both, and the comment didn't ask to remove them.

The 5 orphan blocks check reports (two canopy brackets, two cornice ends, the pig's snout) and the palette tool's moss_block outlier flag were all there in v1. I didn't touch them because the comment didn't mention them.
